text.title: Incident Decision Template — Procedure
text.summary: Seven steps the scribe runs on a live bridge, in the two minutes after the commander speaks: open the record from the incident, write the one-sentence decision, list the options including do-nothing, take the blast radius from the open dashboard, agree the numeric rollback trigger, pin the evidence, commit, then close the loop at the postmortem.

step.name: open-record-on-bridge
step.input: The incident ticket or PagerDuty incident; the time the commander announced the call; the commander's handle.
step.action: Copy `templates/skeleton.md.j2`; fill `trigger.kind: incident`, `trigger.url`, `incident_id`, `decided_at` (the spoken time), `owner` = commander (or the delegate the commander named on the bridge). If the executor is someone else, add the `executor` entry.
step.output: Record opened with trigger and owner.
step.decision-gate: If the bridge has already closed, add `reconstructed: {reconstructed: true, at: now}` before writing anything else (r-record-before-bridge-closes, r-owner-is-commander-or-delegate).

step.name: write-the-decision-sentence
step.action: Write `decision` as one imperative sentence: action, target system, region, when ("Disable the recommendations sidecar in eu-west-1 now."). Read it back on the bridge.
step.decision-gate: "Consider", "maybe", "look into", "should probably", or a second sentence: rewrite before continuing (r-decision-is-one-imperative-sentence).

step.name: list-options-considered
step.input: What was proposed and rejected on the bridge in the last few minutes.
step.action: Add `options_considered` with one line per option: action plus why it was or was not chosen. Always include the "do nothing / keep observing" line with its reason.
step.output: `options_considered` entry with at least two items.
step.decision-gate: Only one option and nobody mentioned waiting: record that as a finding for the postmortem rather than inventing a second option (r-options-considered-min-two).

step.name: quantify-blast-radius
step.input: The dashboard already open on the bridge: error rate, affected request count, affected tenants or regions.
step.action: Write `blast_radius` as systems / regions / tenants plus a number (percent of traffic, req/min, customer count or revenue per minute).
step.decision-gate: No number available: write the count from the alert payload or the log query, never "some users" (r-blast-radius-quantified).

step.name: agree-rollback-trigger
step.input: The metric the bridge is watching; the runbook or the command that undoes the mitigation.
step.action: Agree out loud and record `rollback_trigger` as `metric`, `threshold` (a number), `window` (a duration) and `rollback` (command or runbook URL).
step.decision-gate: The mitigation does not ship until the trigger is numeric (r-rollback-trigger-measurable, fm-02).

step.name: pin-evidence-and-commit
step.input: The dashboard URL with the incident window selected; the alert permalink; the chat message where the decision was announced.
step.action: Add each URL to `evidence[]`, making sure dashboard links carry the pinned time range in the query string; set `review.postmortem_date` and `review.next_review_at` to the postmortem; run `scripts/validate-incident-decision-template.py --file`; commit; set `trigger.committed_at` and `bridge_open_at_commit`.
step.decision-gate: A dashboard URL without `from`/`to` (or equivalent) is replaced before commit; if commit lands more than 2 minutes after the decision, add the `reconstructed` entry (r-evidence-is-timestamped-signal, r-record-before-bridge-closes).

step.name: review-at-postmortem
step.input: The incident timeline; the committed record; the metric history for the rollback trigger.
step.action: At the postmortem fill `review.outcome`: `rollback_trigger_fired`, `blast_radius_matched`, `measured_blast_radius`, `reviewed_at`. Mark the record stale if the postmortem closes without it.
step.decision-gate: `next_review_at` later than the postmortem date is rejected by the validator (r-review-at-postmortem).

list.item: Record validates via `scripts/validate-incident-decision-template.py` with no violation.
`committed_at` minus `decided_at` is at most 2 minutes, or `reconstructed` is present.
`review.outcome` is filled by the postmortem date.
